ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A student named Xiaozan designed an experimental setup to measure ambient temperature using an electronic balance. A thermally conductive cylinder, open at the top, is fixed on a table. A piston with mass $m_{1}=600\mathrm{{g}}$ and cross-sectional area $S=20\mathrm{cm}^{2}$ seals a certain mass of ideal gas within the cylinder. The piston moves without friction against the cylinder wall. A light, rigid rod is supported at its center by a fixed pivot point A. The left end of the rod is vertically connected to the piston via an inextensible string, while the right end is vertically connected to an iron block of mass $m_{2}=1200\mathrm{g}$, which rests on the electronic balance. When the electronic balance reads $600.0\mathrm{g}$, the measured ambient temperature is $T_{1}=300\mathrm{K}$. Given the external atmospheric pressure $p_{0}=1.0{\times}10^{5}\mathrm{Pa}$ and the acceleration due to gravity $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. When the electronic balance reads $400.0\mathrm{g}$, what is the ambient temperature $T_{2}$?
2. What is the maximum ambient temperature $T_{\mathrm{max}}$ that this device can measure?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The attached figure shows a light rod labeled Light rod, with its midpoint supported by a fixed fulcrum A; there is a vertical thin string at each of the left and right ends of the light rod. The left thin string is connected downward to a piston in a cylinder, and the piston is labeled m1; the right thin string is connected downward to an iron block placed on an electronic balance, and the iron block is labeled m2. The fulcrum A is located at the center of the light rod, so the left and right moment arms are equal. Then reason: Let the tensions in the two thin strings be F. The light rod is very light and the fulcrum is at the center, and the left and right moment arms are equal, so from torque equilibrium the tensions at the two ends are equal. When the reading of the electronic balance is M, the support force of the balance on the iron block is N=Mg. Force equilibrium of the iron block: N+F=m2g, so F=m2g-N=(m2-M)g. Force equilibrium of the piston: the upward force of the gas pressure p on the piston is pS, and the tension F in the thin string is also upward; the external atmospheric pressure p0S and the piston weight m1g are downward. Therefore pS+F=p0S+m1g, that is p=p0+(m1g-F)/S. From the constraints of the fixed fulcrum, light rod, and vertical thin strings in the figure, when the iron block is still pressing on the balance and the thin strings are taut, the height of the right end is fixed, the light rod does not rotate, and the height of the left end is also fixed, so the piston height does not change and the gas volume does not change. The cylinder conducts heat, and the gas temperature is equal to the ambient temperature, so the ideal gas satisfies p/T=constant. Given m1=0.600 kg, m2=1.200 kg, S=20 cm^2=2.0×10^-3 m^2, p0=1.0×10^5 Pa. During calibration, M1=0.600 kg, F1=(1.200-0.600)×10=6 N, and m1g=0.600×10=6 N, so p1=p0+(6-6)/S=1.0×10^5 Pa, corresponding to T1=300 K. When M2=0.400 kg, F2=(1.200-0.400)×10=8 N, so p2=1.0×10^5+(6-8)/(2.0×10^-3)=1.0×10^5-1000=9.9×10^4 Pa. Under constant volume, T2=T1·p2/p1=300×(9.9×10^4)/(1.0×10^5)=297 K. When measuring the highest temperature, the increase in temperature causes the gas pressure to increase. From p=p0+(m1g-F)/S, it can be seen that the tension F decreases. The tension cannot be negative, so the limit is F=0, and at this time the balance reading is M=m2. Thus pmax=p0+m1g/S=1.0×10^5+6/(2.0×10^-3)=1.03×10^5 Pa. Therefore Tmax=T1·pmax/p1=300×1.03=309 K.
